utterances.text: Perhaps I can just refresh your memory again, Witness D. What you told the Office of the Prosecutor in relation to the 19th of June was that you were detained at around 4.00 or 5.00 a.m., you were taken to the police station, that at the police station, other men were loaded into the van, two of whom were Albanians, one nicknamed - and if I mispronounce it, I apologise - Zvjezdas who owned a cake shop in Prijedor and the other one named Fejzo. Do you remember telling the Office of the Prosecutor that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct, but I'm referring to the 18th, to the evening of the 18th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have been asking you, Witness D, and if you'd concentrate on the questions, I've been asking you about the 19th of June. Can you please concentrate on that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is correct as for the 19th, but I'm telling you that it was in the evening hours of the 18th that I was taken to the police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll just clarify that. You were collected on the evening of the 18th, you were taken home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... you were sent home in the following morning --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- that you -- and taken back to the police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was subsequent to that that you were taken to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got to Keraterm, is this correct that you were in possession of about 100 Deutsche mark and that money was not taken from you upon your being searched?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not have German marks, and the money that I did have, they did not take away except the cigarettes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I was going to ask you about that. Only cigarettes and a lighter were taken from you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got to Keraterm, how many other people were already there who were detained?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Many.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you help us as to what you mean by "many," please, Witness D?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even ten men detained in a camp is too many, and not to mention hundreds or perhaps a thousand or more. This is really too much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness D, I didn't ask you to give us a speech. Can you just tell us, please - it's quite a simple question - how many people were detained in the camp when you arrived? Blank page inserted to insure pagination corresponds between the French and the English transcripts

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Many.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know whether it's me or whether it's the witness, but I don't think we are making very much progress in getting an answer to this question. It's a proper and relevant question. In my submission, he should answer it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The question is: How many people were detained in the camp when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I cannot know the exact number, and it is a question whether anyone will know the answer to it. Some people were inside, some were outside. There was a mass of people outside. And it is impossible to tell, it is impossible to count them, and impossible to say how --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Can you give us an estimate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it, a few hundred and over a thousand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The personnel who were employed or working as guards in the camp, Witness D, it's right, isn't it, that you were able to observe that they were wearing all sorts of uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that indicate to you that all sorts of different units and different types of people were engaged in guarding Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Different types of units? I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I fear we may have to wait until it's working again, Your Honour. Might I sit down whilst we await that, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It's being checked. The problem has been resolved. You may resume.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. It's come at a moment when I'd like to go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness D, would you accept that your total length of stay at Keraterm was approximately two weeks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you now briefly about somebody called Zoran Zigic. You heard of that person whilst you were in Keraterm; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and seen on a few occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you saw him, is it right that you knew him from before the war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw him, is it right that you saw him dressed not in military uniform but in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And whilst you heard from others that he had mistreated people in Keraterm, you, yourself, saw nothing of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to turn now, please, if we may, to one or two individual incidents. First of all, incidents involving Albanians, please, which took place on the 20th of June. Was one of those who was beaten that night the man who'd been at the police station with you, Zvjezdas, the man with the cake shop or the ice cream shop at the bus station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was one of the reasons why that person was being ill-treated was because of an interest in where his money was, where his valuables were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from the Albanians that you've mentioned, were there many other Albanians at the Keraterm facility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about two more in my room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear of others anywhere else in the -- at Keraterm from other detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and that evening when they beat them, I heard that there were more of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of Serbs who were being detained at Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apart from Jovo Radocaj, no, I was not aware of others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we can now turn to Jovo, the Serb. Would you accept this, that the focus and reason why he was singled out for ill-treatment was because of the suggestion that he had voted for the SDA and/or that he had posters of Alija Izetbegovic at his home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we can put a date on that event, would that be about the third day that you were in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot really say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I can just refresh your memory again from what you told the Office of the Prosecutor, you told them it was about 7.00 or 8.00 p.m. on the third day in Keraterm. Does that refresh your memory, Witness D?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: 7.00 or 8.00, yes, but I also said that I could not really say the date or the day when it happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning now, please, to Drago Tokmadzic, he was Croat; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the reason why he was beaten because he was an active policeman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know. All I know is that when they called him out, or rather when they took him out, that one of them, those who had come after him, said, "Are you the one who beats up children?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You yourself were beaten by a man called Duca Knezevic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know his name at the time, but I heard it from others and I was told it by others who knew him well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's correct, isn't it, that he was not a guard at the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Your Honour, my attention is drawn to the fact that his answer was given was, "Are you the one who beats up Serb children," has appeared on the transcript as lacking the word "Serb".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we take note of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The man, Drago Tokmadzic, died at the camp and was taken away, is it right, in a hearse, a conventional hearse of the kind that we're all familiar with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, was that a question for me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I hope so.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Drago Tokmadzic was taken away in a black van. I could not see whether it was a hearse but I doubt it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, there must be a mistake here in the interpretation, because I wasn't listening to the Bosnian but a hearse could never be explained as a coffin. Because what witness is using the word "coffin" and the learned counsel is using the word "hearse".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thanks for your explanation, Mr. Vucicevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Jovo, was his body removed in a black vehicle belonging to Pasinac Cemetery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it the same vehicle that was used to take Tokmadzic away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: May we go into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to insure pagination corresponds between the French and the English transcripts

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's correct, is it not, Witness D, that on at least one occasion, a doctor came to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from that incident, were there other occasions during your stay at Keraterm when you heard of a doctor being present on the premises?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, a doctor came only once, and I mean Dr. Hasim, but nurses -- Mica Kobas, a male nurse, came on a few times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did the male nurse give treatment to people, dispense medicine, and so on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Some powder, lice powder.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your transfer to Omarska took place on the 4th of July. Were some or all of the people from your district also transferred at the same time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Those from my neighbourhood -- those born in my neighbourhood but lived in other places, they were not transferred.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness D, can you help me about this? During your time as a reserve police officer, did you become aware of the establishment of a second police station in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, how was the new police station which was established, how was it called? What was it called?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Name? I don't know how to put it. The police station became a Serb police station. I don't know if that would be its name. If that's what you would call a name, then you could say that it was called the Serb police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you discover if that police station had command-and-control responsibility for Keraterm and Trnopolje and places like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, as part of your duties as a police officer, know of a man called Zivko Knezevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or become aware of him in connection with Keraterm camp at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not hear of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning now, please, to your being at Manjaca. I'm not sure how to pronounce that. You arrived there on the 5th of August of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 6th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 6th. Was that a place which was being run under the auspices of the International Committee of the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when it was supervised by the ICRC, the International Committee of the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later on, yes. The International Red Cross did come but I don't think that it was under them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that place, is it right that -- where exactly is that in relation to Prijedor? How far away is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prijedor, Banja Luka, and then Banja Luka, Seher, and then to the right up a winding road to the camp. It was a military farm before the war, and it was a military testing ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were released and went off, I think, in a Red Cross convoy to Karlovac; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you help us about this? Were you aware of, whilst you were in Keraterm, of somebody called Bajazit Jakupovic, who was a pilot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The numbers of people who were detained in Keraterm, about which you've talked, would this be correct, they were, whilst you were in Keraterm, fully in the power of the Serb authorities; were they not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you accept that there was nothing to prevent the authorities, the Serb authorities, if they had so chosen, from killing all of you who were detained at Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I doubt very much that something like that existed, but I do not know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as numbers of people detained whilst you were at Omarska, please, Witness D, can you give us an estimate of how many people were there when you were there?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, those people were fully in the power of the Serb authorities whilst detained at Omarska, were they not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, it's right, isn't it, that there was nothing which existed to prevent those same Serb authorities from killing all the prisoners who were in Omarska at any time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there was something like that, I do not know of it, but based on their behaviour, I doubt that anything like that existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Would you just give me a moment, please, Your Honour? Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Rodic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May it please the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Cross-examined by Mr. Rodic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness D, good morning, I am attorney Rodic and I'm a part of the counsel for Damir Dosen. Even though my learned friend Greaves has asked you a number of questions, I will -- I may repeat some of those, but looking for different answers from you. You said that you served in the Yugoslav People's Army in 1983-84, first in Lujbljana and then in Curkovica. Would you please explain to the Trial Chamber what you remember from those days of your national duty regarding the organisation, discipline, subordination in the military?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I -- I have the best possible memories, things that can happen to a young man who is a fresh soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say something about the organisation, discipline, and subordination?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything was organised, everything was under command and control. As I said, I can say only the best.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those who were high in rank were obeyed, the orders were carried out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you completed your service, you became part of the reserve?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you assigned in reserve?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the infantry. I cannot give you the exact code for it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you issued in terms of weapons in the reserve?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: M-48 rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were transferred to the reserve, did you ever have any military exercises and if you were involved in any, what number?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember the numbers. We were once at Manjaca and once at Bukova Kosa, that as you are going to Dubica, and several times in the barracks, and the last time Karac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were on active duty, and I see that you have taken part in the reserve substantially, was there any difference in terms of was the discipline more lax in the reserve?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the reserve, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that a characteristic of the reserve? Can you agree on that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact it may be easier to deal with younger men than with older Blank page inserted to insure pagination corresponds between the French and the English transcripts ones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Regarding the military exercise in September of 1991 when your infantry unit took part, can you tell me how did it look at that time? What was it like in light of the conflicts already taking place in the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything was regular except for some unusual things. We were given much more military equipment, we could take as much as we wanted, and different type of weapons. Perhaps that would be the difference in relation to the previous exercises.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But all this was turned in after the exercise was over?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just the weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were already asked and you responded that in October 1991, you were called up for mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you stated a precise reason. Was that the only reason while you refused to be called up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the fratricidal fighting and the reasons for it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But after that you said that you were one of the initiators of the rally in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many people were there, approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: A couple of thousand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did that rally end?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the broadcast on the radio, that is the speech of the president of the municipality, we simply dispersed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did something happen after the rally, something similar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, was there a counter-rally held, organised by the Serb and the non-Serb population after this rally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the call-up which you refused to respond to, you were never called up again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, except over the radio.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But can you tell me, did you suffer any consequences because of your refusal to respond to the call-up and because of the organisation of the rally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know that at that time a refusal to respond to a call-up and asking others to not respond was considered a criminal act?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you afraid of what the consequences may have been for your actions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was a large mass of people there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time when this was going on regarding the rally, was Bosnia a part of the -- of Yugoslavia or was it independent?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was independent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your opinion, when did it become independent?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give us an exact day or approximate date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall it now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you worked in the iron mining company and that due to the war, there was not enough work.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The situation in which you find yourself in that period of time had nothing to do with the ethnic situation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that period, say up to May 1992, except for the problems at checkpoints, the controls and so on, did Serbs and Muslims both continue to go to work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As -- and the period of late 1991 early 1992, during that period were there Croats and Muslims who were members of the JNA units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were Croats and Muslims in the JNA units, that is, in the Territorial Defence units at that time, were there some -- did some of these Croats and Muslims take part in the fighting, in the wars in other parts of the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me, until the end of April 1992 were there any major problems in the territory of Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know that power changed on the 30th of April 1992. At that time did you know the reason, was that explained why this took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The reason that was given was that the parties could not agree on the division of power and that for that reason, the SDS was taking over everything in their own hands, and this was a public announcement on the radio.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you be more specific? Which parties were unable to agree, and they could not agree on what powers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: SDS, HDZ, and SDA, and it regarded the division of power in the Prijedor municipality, the appointment of managers to certain companies and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the problem was in the execution? The power was already in place, the president of the municipality, the vice-president, and they were all members of these parties, so it was the implementation of the decisions that was problematic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and some of the positions had not been filled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell me about the takeover of power. Did it result in any casualties, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the takeover, I don't -- I did not hear of any casualties during the takeover.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you spoke about your call-up to join the reserve police, you said that you were called for an interview with Rade Zekan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that an active-duty policeman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that occasion, was Aziz Aliskovic with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I excluded Aziz, because he stayed in the car while I talked to Rade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that moment was Aziz also an active-duty police officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me when and where were you issued a reserve police uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was issued it in Prijedor, in the police station, one day before the takeover of power in town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have the right size, given your height?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was difficult.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell me, regarding Esad Islamovic and Drago Tokmadzic, you said that they were fired. Do you know how it happened and why it happened? Was it because they did -- they refused to continue to be in the police after the takeover of power?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know what I heard from Esad, and I also talked to Drago about it. A similar thing happened to both of them. The colleagues with whom they had worked, at about the same time - this has happening in two different locations - turned weapons on them, and told that they had to leave their posts and they had to go home, and from there on the Serbs were taking over everything, and that it would be an exclusively Serb police from there on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they tell you when exactly this happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: 2.00 or 3.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this was already early on the 30th of April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or the 31st.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that they nevertheless continued to work in the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you explain this situation if previously they had been told that non-Serbs had no place in the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, sir, there was still the civil police. And what I mean by that is that, regardless of their ethnicity, they could work there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This police in Ljubija, was it composed of Serbs as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were called up to join the reserve police, did anybody mention as an obstacle, or as some kind of a problem, your organisation of the rally and your refusal to join?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know what reasons were given for the increased number of police officers so that also the reserves were activated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the steadily -- the reasons was the steadily worsening situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me, have you heard of Milutin Cadjo? And what did Cadjo do after the takeover in the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had heard of Cadjo even before, while he was still a policeman in Ljubija, but I wouldn't be able to tell you what exactly he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a commander of the police in Ljubija before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the war, the commander was Baja Bjekic. And before Baja?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, can you tell me how long your cross-examination will be? How much longer?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will need more than one hour, perhaps one hour and 15, one hour 20 minutes, because the witness mentioned our client the most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I appreciate that. And Mr. Vucicevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wish I could answer your question but I can't because, first, the cross-examination of Mr. Rodic has not been finished, and after I get that information, I might be able to give you some estimate. But it seems to me that the witness is rather informative and some questions are -- I don't know how much the witness is going to answer, so I cannot give you answer to the question. I wish I could but I can't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, as I said at the beginning of the day, we are making every effort to conclude this witness's testimony today. I think, with the cooperation of the interpreters, we can go for another ten minutes. Another ten minutes before taking the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that on the 1st of May, 1992 in the afternoon, you first started working as a reserve policeman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned during your examination-in-chief that you were refreshing your handling of the weapons when you were first issued it at the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to insure pagination corresponds between the French and the English transcripts

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you ever had --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Would you repeat the question, counsel? Repeat the last question?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My last question was whether you had any previous contact with the police service before.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We could not hear the witness' answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you briefly describe that first working day when you reported to the police station and were assigned your tasks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned already that all members of the reserve force went out together with active-duty policemen so my first day there was more or less like this. A vehicle from the station came to my home, since the checkpoint is -- was away from my home, and together with an active-duty policeman, Ismet Taras, we drove to the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And before you left for the checkpoint, did anyone tell you anything about the task before you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was who?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, who told me? Ismet did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ismet who?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Taras.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he was what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Active-duty policeman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But do you understand what I'm asking? Was he just a policeman on the beat, a patrolman, or did he have a rank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was just a plain police officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when he told you about your task, did he sound like transmitting to you the order of somebody who was above him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chief of the police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was Branko Bjekic, was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And with regard to the powers of policemen, their rights and duties, in terms of the arrest procedure or the procedure of taking under custody, procedure of detention, in terms of the official record of a possible criminal report, did you undergo any training there at all? Did you receive any instructions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I had no training, and the same holds true of the fact that we were not authorised to either bring somebody under custody or perhaps collect fines, or even we were not entitled to even any fuel because we were simply cut off from Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I asked you a moment ago, it did not have to do with the situation in Prijedor or Ljubija. What I meant was you, as a policeman, who is for the first time working for the police as a reserve policeman, and things that I just listed are some of the things that the policemen learn at school or attend courses, have special training. So that was the gist of my question. Did you have any training, any instructions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, may I ask what is the relevance of that to the question of the guilt or innocence of your client, the scope of his training as a reserve policeman? How does that affect the guilt or innocence of your client?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think it is of quite a high relevance because the Chamber and the Prosecution compare Witness D who was a reserve policeman like our client, like our accused, and we wish -- and it is an attempt to show the real status, the real knowledge they had of the police, of the police rights and duties, a trained policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: If I may suggest --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just, Mr. Rodic -- please go ahead, but please try and take it very quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour. Just one more thing. The indictment says, "Also as active-duty policeman, Damir Dosen, Dusan Fustar, Dragan Kolundzija independently of this were bound to apply laws in force in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina and protect life and property of civilian persons."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, perhaps we'll take the break now. We'll take the break now. Before we do that, however, Judge May is going to raise something with Mr. Vucicevic in relation to the matters he mentioned yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Vucicevic, yesterday you raised the question of the documents which you had obtained from the UN, and you referred to some correspondence with me as the then Presiding Judge in this matter. It's right that there was correspondence, or at least you informed of what had happened. You did not send us, of course, the documents, but you sent us the correspondence with the UN, and we've also heard from the UN on this subject. I've now had the opportunity of refreshing my memory of that correspondence and the position is this: That you, of course, cannot, because of the conditions which you accepted, disclose that correspondence or any documents that you discovered, without the consent, the written consent of the UN if you want to put them into evidence. Now, that being so, the right course to adopt is for you to indicate to the UN those documents that you intend to adduce in evidence, and following the conditions which they have laid down, seek their consent in order to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe the confidentiality letter that was sent to me and that I have accepted in principle was there to prevent any wide distribution of the material, not to undermine the future peacekeeping operation of the United Nations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: However, this Court being United Nations body, I believe the office -- I don't have document in front of me and you know you do have advantage having refreshed your memory and I haven't, but I believe at the discretion of the Trial Chamber to accept some of the documents in the close session, but not of the United Nations whether they would agree or not agree whether this -- this is becoming a travesty, then, of the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Vucicevic, go back and read the document which is quite plain as to the course which you should follow if you wish to adduce these documents in evidence. The first thing you must do is to refer them to the UN. Read the letter which you have agreed to, follow those conditions, and then you can tell us what happened. But just remind me, how many documents is it that you want to produce?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I don't know that I -- after your previous ruling, and am I at liberty to say anything?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just answer the question. Is it 17 or 27? I forget, just tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: There was 25 to 27, those were banker -- hold on, you know, that's not -- I didn't finish, you know, what I had to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Vucicevic, don't interrupt the Court. Don't be impertinent. Now, it's 25 or 27. Follow the instructions of the UN, and then you might be able to adduce them into evidence. But you have agreed to those conditions, read them again, and follow them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll take the adjournment until 2.30. You are reminded, Witness D, not to discuss your evidence with anybody including members of the Prosecution team. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.15 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, just a second. Mr. Vucicevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I have a special request from the interpreters that when you speak, you should wait until the other person who is speaking also finishes, so as to prevent overlapping. They are having immense difficulty in the interpreting when you're speaking, so please take that into account.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Also if counsellor could be advised to put on the microphone when speaking?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Rodic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Just before my friend does, may I just make one other observation? I understand my friend Mr. Vucicevic is fluent in both languages and therefore doesn't need to wear headphones, but if he wears his headphones, he'll be able to hear when the translator is finished and that might give him his cue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I did notice that he doesn't wear the headphones. It would help if you wore the headphones.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm extremely grateful to the suggestion. I tried but the thought process while I'm thinking, if I'm listening too, then it's difficult to concentrate. So as I said, I think it would be a little easier if I'm just looking at the transcript. When transcript is given, I start with the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. Thanks very much. I'm sure we will do better. Yes, Mr. Rodic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness D, before the break, we left off with questions about the reserve police officers. As a reserve police officer, did you receive any salary?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had no remuneration with respect to that activity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Neither did anybody else from the reserve, in the reserve force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain in some detail the structure of the police station where you worked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the last day of my duty, it was mixed, and the day after I left, it was still a multiethnic organisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I were asked -- if I asked you about the structure, that is the number of police officers there and their structure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would not be easy for me to do that. For a while some police officers did not come to work at all. Some were on duty but not coming to the police station, so I really could not explain it well for you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But could you be able to tell me with respect to the tasks given to the police officers in your police station? Did they provide security for certain facilities? What would have fallen within the scope of their activities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tasks of the reserve forces at that time and the police itself consisted of trying to calm down the population and controlling the weapons and so on. Blank page inserted to insure pagination corresponds between the French and the English transcripts

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here you mentioned that specifically your task was at a checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The other policemen in the police station were also assigned to various checkpoints or assigned to duties of providing security to various facilities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police men from the Miska Glava village were there; and those from the Surkovac were in Surkovac; in Rasko, from Rasko. We from Donja Ljubija were at Donja Ljubija. Whereas the active police officers coordinated their work with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that involve and include, in addition to the tasks at checkpoint, patrols?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did reserve police officers also go on these patrols?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you tell me about the structure of the police station in terms of its command structure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander was Baja Bjekic. His deputy was Komosar, another Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, were there any shift leaders, duty officers, patrol heads?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were patrol officers and, we who were in the reserve, went along with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understood that, but you mentioned Commander Bjekic, Deputy Komosar. In addition to those, were there the duties that I just mentioned to you, were --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you tell me whether the reserve policemen in your station had any ranks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're referring now to the reserve police officers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know some of these ranks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Corporal, sergeant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any ranks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The ranks which you mentioned were the lowest ranks in this hierarchy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Another question in this area: Could you make any significant decisions about your work without a commander or whoever was your leader?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned that you had heard about the incident at Hambarine where there was an exchange of fire between the people manning the checkpoint and some Serbs who were in a vehicle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who was manning that checkpoint at Hambarine?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know who was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Aziz was in charge of it, but I don't know who was on duty at the time except from what I've heard, but I'm trying only to limit myself to what I know 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is what is also convenient to me.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it is not convenient to me, because I don't consider these questions to be significant and I find them very exhausting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let the Trial Chamber decide on that. Could you tell me, at that point, do you know whether Aziz Aliskovic was an active duty police officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you tell me specifically what your task was at the checkpoint? What were you supposed to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Control vehicles, and calming down of the tense situation in the population, among the population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you have any authority to use weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just one additional question relating to Hambarine. Did they, in the ultimatum that they had issued, did they ask for the surrender of Aliskovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that in May 1992 you were transferred to Donja Ljubija as a police officer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This happened in spite of the takeover of power and the armed conflict at Hambarine.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any position there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you were first detained 10 days after you were relieved of duty as a police officer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me approximately when that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: In June 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the time when Drago Tokmadzic and Esad Islamovic were arrested?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two or three days before my arrest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your first arrest or your second arrest?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the night of the 18th and 19th. So that means it was before the 19th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you were arrested for the second time on the 18th.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A little while ago you mentioned that you were first arrested about 10 days after being relieved of duty.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: My first detention was on the 18th of June when I was arrested and brought to the police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And before that you were never detained.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you're putting a 10-day period, that would mean that you left the reserves around the 8th of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did say it was in early June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me, do you know anything about the attack on Prijedor, how many people were involved?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, just what I heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell me, do you know that Esad Islamovic continued to work after the attack on Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you something about his work on identification and arrest of persons involved in that attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today in your examination-in-chief you mentioned that Serb extremists were criminals, that this is how you referred to them. I would like to know whether there were extremists on the other side too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that Komosar said that he would stay behind to prevent the entry of the Serb extremists in the police station. That meant that we who were Croats and Muslims had to leave the police station and that the Serbs would come, and that among those Serbs, he would select those who were better. And as far as the Muslim extremists are concerned, if we are referring to the thieves and criminals, I know of those, who had criminal records from before, who had convictions earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who Slavko Acimovic is, from Tukovi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have heard of him but I did not know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you hear about him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: That he was one of the organisers in the attempt of liberating Prijedor. Blank page inserted to insure pagination corresponds between the French and the English transcripts

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of Halim Mesic from Cela?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of Mesic called Hadja from Raskovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've heard of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you hear of him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that they took part in the attempt to liberate Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a Jasmin Alisic called Jama from Tukovi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you hear of him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he was a butcher there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know anything else about him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of Kemo called Divljak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know about him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everybody knew Kemo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber does not know. Could you explain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kemo had been in prisons before the war. This is what I know about him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these individuals commanders of certain units that took part in the attack on Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned a person named Ikanovic whom you heard he was killed. This is in relation to the people at the stadium.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was at the start of the search.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know his first name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Smajo Ikanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said Smajo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One of the person who worked -- persons who worked with you was Milan Curguz from Kalje [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know this man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, but he worked there after me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know that he brought food to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know to whom he was bringing food?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that once he brought it for me, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have any problem in entering Keraterm and delivering this to you and others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Simo Savic, active policeman from Ljubija?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the attack on Hambarine, I think he could no longer come to work. That is, after the Serb takeover in Prijedor, he transferred to work in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why was he unable to come to work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to move to some questions about the organisation of security at Keraterm. I would like to know your personal impression based on your stay and your experience, which would include both your military and police experience. Did this look to you like an organised unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had it been an organised unit, things that happened would not have happened. And if we look at the deployment of the sentry posts, the machine-gun nests, and the way we were kept under lock, I think it was fairly well organised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm interested in is the organisation, in a sense of order and discipline, subordination, relationship between the subordinates and their superiors and so on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the respect went, I think what was respected was the law of the might, of those who were mightier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the commanders order beatings of certain detainees or did these beatings took place -- take place on the will of the guards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear any commander issue orders to beat any detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know whether any of the detainees reported to anyone that they had been beaten or mistreated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because they were afraid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were they afraid of specifically?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: The guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean a guard that had beaten him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: And everybody else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How would that coincide with what I have asked you before? In other words, could you link those two things?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not quite understand. I don't know what you're trying to hear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If the fear prevented them from reporting, that is, the fear of guards, would that imply that the guards would have been punished had it been found out that they were -- had they been beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a very difficult question for me. A commander or guard in this particular case is one and the same. A commander could only be identified by the respect or compliance of the guards, but let me try to give you an example.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: For instance, Banovic could only be disciplined or curbed by Kajin because he was afraid of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That would confirm what you said, that it was really the law of the mightier that ruled?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spent time both at Keraterm, Omarska, and Manjaca. Could you make a comparison between Keraterm and Omarska? What was more difficult?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Keraterm fewer people were killed than in Omarska. And as far as conditions are concerned, they were about the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And with respect to the guards' shifts and the organisation of security?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were similar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a command structure at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you counted the interrogators who interrogated us, yes. But the same thing existed in Keraterm even though I did not go in for questioning, but it was similar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in what sense do you mean "in relation to the interrogators"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Keraterm there was a camp commander and shift commanders. At Omarska there was a camp commander and shift commanders, except Omarska was larger and had more interrogators.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Zeljko Meakic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Miroslav Kvocka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mlado Radic called Krkan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these men those who were part of the structure there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two were shift commanders, and the first name you mentioned was the camp commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they all active-duty police officers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know of Krkan, but not about the other two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you now make comparison for me between Omarska, Keraterm, and Manjaca? First of all, do you know what Manjaca was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a military farm and also a military training camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we call it "camp" like Keraterm and Omarska, was that under the military control?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give me a comparison of the conditions based on your experience?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: The most important thing was that we were beaten less. If a barn can be called adequate conditions in comparison to Omarska and Keraterm, it was fairly satisfactory, but only in comparison to Keraterm and Omarska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And with respect to the organisation, was that more professional than in the other two places?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: By far.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the beginning of your direct examination, you told the Court about your arrival in Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said it was the 19th of June.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Early morning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which shift was on duty that day, or which ones of the guards or perhaps their leaders did you see then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you familiar with the organisation of shifts in Keraterm; when did they start, when did they go off duty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know it then. I learned about it subsequently. Anyone could enter the Keraterm camp and at any time wearing any uniform, only naturally, of course, if he was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear about at what times did the shifts change?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was sometime in the afternoon and in the morning, late afternoon and the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So which means every 12 hours, would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many shifts were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did you learn about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how many shifts were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were asked about Kajin, you said his name was Damir Dosenovic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That his brother was Drasko Dosenovic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that you said that you knew Damir for some eight or nine years before the war, and that you met him two or three times?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me correct myself. Dosen, Drasko Dosen, Damir Dosen. And even before that, as of the 1980s when we started school, I knew about him. I had heard about him even though we were not in touch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With whom were you not in touch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: With Damir. Blank page inserted to insure pagination corresponds between the French and the English transcripts

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that you never talked with him and that, as we call it, by sight?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the "Hello", "Hello" basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is Damir Dosen younger than you are?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it is with Drasko Dosen that you attended the same grade.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you call him, Drasko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I called him Drasko or Kajin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Kajin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kajin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the same nickname was used for both?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Only for the record, because it says, "Kajin, Kajin," and let us correct. Was Damir called Kajin too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned a guard called Pilip?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And since when did you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the school days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you friends?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you say -- could we say that you know him well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And with regard to your arrival in Keraterm, you testified -- you stated earlier that that day, around 7.00 or 8.00 in the evening, you recognised some of the guards on the night shift and you say that every -- that there were 12-hour shifts and that they were "Damir Dosenovic called Kajin, elder brother Drasko Dosenovic, with whom I went to school together, Mladen Pilipovic called Pilip, my fellow worker, and Dusan Madza who also went to school with me"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is. They all were on the same shift and I learnt that their shift leader was Kajin.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I saw him assign tasks to other guards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please be more specific about those tasks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was some papers or lists or files, one could see him have them. Others did not have any such thing. As for authority, whether was it fear or was it rank, I wouldn't know. Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you eye-witness some event, an incident in the camp when Kajin tried to restrain Banovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us something more about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: On one occasion when Banovic was about to beat somebody with a baseball bat, I don't know whom, I saw Kajin come up to him and call him, and after a brief altercation, they went together to the kiosk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you don't know what happened then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on that occasion, did he prevent Banovic from ill-treating somebody?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your examination-in-chief yesterday and today -- or rather yesterday, you testified, "After I came to Keraterm, I went to the first room" and there that you met some acquaintances. Then you said, "In front of Room 4, I recognised Drago Tokmadzic and Esad Islamovic." And they told you that it was full but to put up there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less. In Room 1 they told me that they were also over there, and I recognised many, many people, many people I knew, and then I went to Room number 4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is what you said today, that you were told that Drago and Eso were in Room 4?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before that you stated that after you arrived in Keraterm, you headed for Room 1, where you saw Bajram Jakupovic and, "After that I moved to Room 2, where I saw two relatives of mine. And then I heard Drago Tokmadzic and Esad Islamovic call out to me from Room 4, so I went to them." Now, which of these -- this is true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All I can say is that your earlier statement to the investigators, to the OTP investigator is what I just read out.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it could be a mistake. I went to Room 1, and the two relatives whom you mentioned were in Room 1, and then by Room 2 and 3, I went to Room 4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the -- these task assignment lists and other things that you mentioned, could you tell us where were you on such occasions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it depended on the situation in the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But during his shifts could you come out freely?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not always.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the first day when you arrived in Keraterm that there were very many people outside?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that there were people who had burned from being in the sun?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I should like to ask you the following: You testified here about how a Serb, Jovo Radocaj, was brought?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the examination-in-chief today, you said that Jovo Radocaj on the second day of your stay at Keraterm was brought sometimes in night hours, that he was put in "my room." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What I said was that Jovo was brought in the early days of my imprisonment in late afternoon hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The record says, "It was on my second day in Keraterm." In your earlier statement, you say "on the third day of my stay" in the evening hours, you saw them bring Jovo Radocaj near the weigh bridge. What is correct of this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stated the order in which I put things are correct. The date could be mistaken maybe, I simply -- my memory fails me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But if you remember that you were brought on the 19th, then we have two different times here, one that Jovo Radocaj was brought on the second day of your detention, and according to a previous statement, it was the third day of your arrival. So it is not difficult to calculate the date if we know the 19th; wouldn't you agree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: That it was quite possible that he was brought on the very next day or the second day or the third day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that he was brought during Kajin's shift?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you when you watched it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between the Room 3 -- Rooms 3 and 4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was -- where were Kajin and Jovo Radocaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the reception office in Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please be more specific?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Facing Rooms 1 and 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it next to the weigh bridge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.
