utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you be more specific as to the distance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between the bunker and the weigh bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how far were you from them, roughly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: 20 to 30 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there other people between you in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in front of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not in front of your eyes or at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in front of my eyes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said today that Jovo Radocaj was put in your room. By this you mean Room 4?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said today that Jovo was called out that same evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that the voice which called him out was Kajin's voice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you at that moment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: By the door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Outside or inside?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you locked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who unlocked the room? After Jovo left the room, did you see who it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you then recognise Kajin's voice, how did you know it was Kajin's voice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when somebody talks with somebody in America over the phone, one can recognise it and know who it is, so that is how I knew who it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you clarify this? I really failed to understand you. I asked you how did you know that it was his voice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew it. Just as we could recognise -- know when Ziga would come to the camp and start yelling and shouting. We would not see him, but we always knew it was Ziga.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But a while ago you said that you never talked with Kajin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that the next day you saw a bloody stain on the wall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that it looked round to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain where it was in terms of windows, doors?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entrance to Room 4 was -- it was about a metre, metre away from the door -- at the height of a metre and a half.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to go back to the previous question, it was only your second day in the camp. How was it that you could already know -- tell Kajin's voice from other voices?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was the second or the third day, but the fact that I never talked with Kajin does not mean that I never heard him speak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I pointed out those inconsistencies to you that today you said it from the second day, and in your statement you said it was the third day. Now I will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, I just wanted to ask the witness a question. Witness D, you said the fact that you never talked with Kajin doesn't mean that you never heard him speak. About how many times did you hear him speak prior to this incident in those two or three days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first day in the camp, in the evening, Kajin's shift came on, and then I heard him several times. And I recognised him immediately because I knew his voice from before because we'd come across one another in the town, so that that was enough for me to conclude that that was his voice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did you hear him speak on another occasion apart from that first time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the first time in the camp or before the camp?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, in the camp.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, several times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And prior to the incident involving Jovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, how much longer do you have?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another ten minutes, perhaps, Your Honour, maybe even less.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Kajin at the point when Eso and Drago were being carried into the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anyone near to you when you were carrying them in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After entering the room, you said that you lost consciousness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: After a brief period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you now tell me when you carried Eso and Drago in the room, were you locked in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who did that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After a brief period you said that Pilip came to the room.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who let Pilip in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: He went and fetched the key.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that he went to get the key?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he called me out for the first time, I did not want to respond. Our joint friend was there, and he said -- he told me that I could not get up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My apologies. Did he call you from outside?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know where he went to get the key?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain to me how Pilip, when he came to the room after having previously called you out from outside, how he knew that you had been beaten when nobody had called you out the previous night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he perhaps explain to you that situation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies. Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness D, thank you for your evidence. Your Honours, I have concluded my examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness D, I'd like to ask you a question. About how many days was it after you heard Kajin beating Jovo that you yourself were beaten and you called out for Kajin too, you said, "Pilip, Kajin, they are killing me."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how many days went by, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But you still -- you had enough confidence in Kajin to have called upon him to help you, notwithstanding what you said you had heard or seen in relation to Kajin beating Jovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Why was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we were to talk a bit longer about this, there were Serbs who, on the one side, helped, and on the other side did bad things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. I will not take it any further. Mr. Vucicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Vucicevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness D, my name is Dusan Vucicevic and I represent Dragan Kolundzija. You have testified in direct that you were put on the paid leave from your enterprise where you were employed. Could you tell us when did it happen; a year, month, or perhaps a week of the month if you know? I won't ask you for a date.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the end of 1991 until May or April, but perhaps I even received one salary in coupons the way salaries were distributed in that period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why were you put on paid leave, and I will sort of make it short, was it because there was no work or any other reason?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe because there was no work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... employed people of all nationalities: Muslims, Serbs, Croats and the others; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And isn't it true that paid leave was a benefit that was granted to all people in your enterprise regardless of their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also testified that you were invited to join reserve police unit in Ljubija. Could you tell the Court the date when that offer was made to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Late April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In cross-examination that was conducted by Mr. Rodic, you indicated that you took the uniform from the police station in Prijedor on 29th of April. I'm using that as a reference point. How many days prior to your putting on a uniform was this offer made?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps a week before that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your direct you testified that the jurisdiction of Ljubija police station was extending as far as Tukovi; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Usher, could you please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness D, you already identified this map. Could you please Blank page inserted to insure pagination corresponds between the French and the English transcripts state what is the distance from Ljubija to Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: 11 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you draw in your own hand on this map what was the territory that was covered by or that was the jurisdiction of police station in Ljubija?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So basically the statement that you have given to the Court that jurisdiction of Ljubija when you testified on your direct was misleading, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, the area that are covered -- that were covered by the Donja Ljubija police station are not shown on this map at all. I can only name them for you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, sir, that wasn't the question. Thank you. Mr. Usher -- Your Honours, here is the bigger map of the region. I would like the witness to take a look at it. Not presenting it as the evidence at this time, just want him to refresh his recollection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, the Prosecution will object on grounds of relevance. It's our position that many of these areas have already been covered, and it's difficult for us to see a connection to the specific charges for which the accused are on trial here today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Vucicevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness has testified that he, just shortly before the beginning of the at least political hostilities, so-called power takeover in Prijedor, was solicited to become a policeman in Ljubija. He has manned a certain checkpoints and in manning those checkpoints, he said that the jurisdiction of Ljubija station was all the way to Tukovi, and that he was a member of the police station and he was in a certain areas. I just want to establish how big of the area of what did he have jurisdiction in. That's all. I think it's highly relevant. First, it's relevant as to his recollection --

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: And also it's relevant --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We will allow it. Try to deal with it quickly, background material.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I will.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you put it on the ELMO, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: My apologies. No. In this area, the -- this map, the area covered by the Ljubija police station is not shown.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please put the map on ELMO so that we can see Prijedor? Could you move the map higher? A little more higher? And toward the 10.00, if you look at the screen clockwise, Ljubija on that map, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is but I really cannot see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, perhaps you will clearer see it on this map. Could you show him this map? Would you move it up a little higher? Move up a little higher and enhance, please. Enhance a little more. Okay. No, no, pull it down. Pull it down. That's proper enhancement. That's it. Just keep it right there. Okay, sir, could you show us where is Ljubija here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you see there Carakovo, don't you, on that map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you show us on that map where is part of municipality of Prijedor which is called Tukovi? It is right next to Prijedor. It's not -- it's not shown there, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps we can then take that one off and put the Prosecutor's map and then, you know, I would kindly show it to the witness because clear indicated, I would show it to the court there are three maps with different localities and the witness is confused, and I understand it's been a long day, but maybe we can start with the first map. You see where Prijedor is indicated in the map, Witness D, and there is clearly written "Tukovi" right there. You see that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And then in the lower, left-hand corner, there is right there highlighted for you, that says "Ljubija," right down here. It says "Donja Ljubija." And could you pull that map just a little bit higher? And there is another place -- just keep it there. Don't move it any more at all, please. And there is Ljubija. And isn't it correct that police station that you were solicited for is located in Ljubija, right where you're showing right now, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And isn't it -- you testified already that Ljubija is part of Prijedor municipality. You said that. Isn't it part of opstina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And town of Prijedor is located and indicated in the biggest letter on that map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So since you said that territory of that police station of Ljubija cover went all the way to Tukovi, that was incorrect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, sir, I did not decide how far it would extend but I know not only Tukovi. If you find -- if you locate Tomasica, we shall be able to see further.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] Thank you. Who was the commanding officer in the -- in the police station, Prijedor 1, at the time that you were offered reserve police duties?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified in your direct that after the elections of December of 1990 were held, there was some dispute among the leaders, between SDA and SDS, about divisional authorities, and perhaps you didn't get a chance to finish. Which position was that dispute all about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question that you want to ask me, who was the chief of police or who was the commander in the police?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who do you -- are you familiar with the name Hasan Talundzic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was the chief of police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Vucicevic, just to say that we are not to take for granted the interpreters. And with their cooperation, we will go on to 4.15. Continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Mr. Talundzic superior to both officers that offered you reserve police position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any conversation -- strike it. You mentioned also -- I just want to get who was a commander at what time in Ljubija. You mentioned a Serb and you mentioned a Muslim. Serb was Zekan and I believe Bjekic was a Muslim, if I am correct. Is that right? Or Croatian?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not even warm. You are not even getting warm. Baja Bjekic, a Croat, was a police commander and the deputy commander from the reserve force was Komosar, a Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... what function or what rank did Mr. Zekan have and Mr. Aliskovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when they talked to you, they were in uniform, were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you testified earlier that you could clearly recognise the ranks on the police officers. So is it your testimony when you talked to them and they offered you position in the police that you didn't notice their ranks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I say is I don't know which ranks they had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... later on what positions did they have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So who was the one that had authority to accept you in police service? Was that Aziz, was that Zekan, or somebody else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was Mr. Bjekic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did that appointment take place? Did he check your background? Did you have to fill out a questionnaire, or you just had a conversation with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an interview.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that conversation, did he send you to Prijedor to take --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- your rifle and uniform.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was issued with a rifle in the station at Ljubija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you went to Prijedor immediately after you finished conversation with him, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the fact is that you became reserve policeman on 29th of April 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... was to be dispatched at a checkpoint. That's what you already testified.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, my first duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you came back from Prijedor, you reported to Mr. Bjekic and he sent you to the checkpoint; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just tell us how long -- what is the time span between you getting the uniform and receiving your first assignment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: A couple of days. Let me repeat --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... to finish this. --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did -- so that means that Serb power takeover in Prijedor already took place; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I went to -- on duty for the first time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do being a reserve policeman in those first few days, if anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a good question. We sat at the checkpoint and did nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that was a point by the gas station, is that so? Because you testified that your first post -- on the checkpoint at the gas station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The railway station next to the bus terminal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So this is the first time that we hear about this checkpoint by the bus station or by the railroad station; isn't that true? We haven't heard it in the direct or any cross-examination that you answered to so far.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember if I mentioned the petrol pump ever or this checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Vucicevic --

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: I have a lot more, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, yes. We can't go beyond 4.15. Mr. Mundis, the Chamber was aware of some difficulties the witness had. What is your position? Will the witness be available tomorrow or will some arrangement have to be made for him to come another day?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, at the moment, I'm not in a position to answer that question. I can certainly make some inquiries and perhaps get back to both Defence counsel and to the Chamber's legal officer. The question involves the witness' employer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Witness D, would you like to say something in relation to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I shall be happy to stay tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That answers that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That answers the question. We'll take the adjournment now. Witness D, you are not to discuss your evidence with anybody and that includes members of the Prosecution team. We will resume at 9.30 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 28th day of March, 2001 at 9.30 a.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
